checks.name: A3-single-live-file-composition
checks.summary: The live exercise is one new file, internal/api/live_dogfood_test.go, package api_test, one top-level TestFoundationPreviewLocalDogfood with seventeen ordered subtests named exactly after what they exercise: environment-identifiers, the twelve cap-<capability-id> exercises, channel-break-and-resume, promotability-negative, promotability-positive and ledger-snapshot. It builds cmd/control-plane with go build into t.TempDir(), starts it with runner.ProcessSupervisor in its own process group on 127.0.0.1 against a real Firestore emulator, and stops it deterministically on cleanup, reusing internal/api/live_local_test.go's helpers (repoRootForLiveTest, freeLocalPort, waitForHealthz, exhaustWriteBudgetOrFail). There is no fixed sleep, no wall-clock dependence and no dependence on another test's order; readiness and process death are bounded polls on observable conditions and every subtest carries a context deadline. The one goroutine the file starts is the supervised child's own run, joined before its subtest returns, because a live child cannot be acted on while in flight without one. internal/api/live_local_test.go was not edited and nothing was moved out of it.

checks.name: A7-backlog-visibility-exercise
checks.summary: cap-backlog-visibility was exercised and did NOT pass in full. What held: GET /v1/requirements?page_size=1 returned exactly one row and a next_cursor; GET /v1/requirements?page_size=100 returned every Requirement this run captured; GET /v1/queue/summary returned counts by requirement status and by increment status and an active execution count that agree with what this run itself created, computed from the run's own captures rather than from a constant, and by_requirement_status summed to the reported requirements total. What did not hold, measured rather than argued: the cursor does not work. GET /v1/requirements with the next_cursor the route itself handed out returned HTTP 400 invalid_request. internal/store/firestore's RequirementsPage orders by firestore.DocumentID and then calls StartAfter(collectionPath + "/" + key); the Go client treats a string cursor for DocumentID as a document id and appends it to the collection path again, so the emulator refuses the query. That is escalation E22-11 and it lives in a prohibited path, so it is recorded and not fixed. Separately recorded as a shortfall and not as a failure of the success condition: the declared user action 'filter by related Repository' has no implementation -- GET /v1/requirements?repository_id=does-not-exist returned the same 2 rows as the unfiltered page (E22-7).

checks.name: A12-channel-break-and-resume
checks.summary: The M5 completion condition 'break the Preview on purpose and resume a Requirement on the previous Stable' was satisfied at the Loop channel layer. Two real binaries of cmd/control-plane were built: the good one from the repository tree and the broken one from a copy of the tree in t.TempDir() with one deliberate defect applied to the copy only -- internal/api/api.go: the authenticated POST dispatch returns HTTP 500 deliberate_dogfood_defect before reaching any handler, so every POST /v1/... fails on that build. Both were installed as real signed bundles through update.InstallRecorded with a test-generated ephemeral ed25519 keypair, and a bundle signed by a different key was refused, so the signature check really runs. update.Switch routed the preview channel and then the stable channel at the good version, the process actually served was the one the channel symlink resolved to, and a Requirement was captured while the stable channel served. update.Switch then pointed the preview channel at the broken version; the failure was observed over real HTTP as 500 deliberate_dogfood_defect on capture and a Runner claim against the broken Preview also failed with 500. update.Switch then returned the preview channel to the previously verified good version, the prior target was not deleted, and the Requirement captured before the break was still present under the restored build in the same Firestore emulator canonical state and advanced to a terminal execution status of succeeded with one real claude invocation. This is a Loop channel rollback and resume at the self-host grade release-contract.md section 3 anticipates while D1 is unpassed; it is NOT a Release Contract Stable release. The signing key was ephemeral and test-generated, so no claim is made about key management (V2-034 owns that). update.Install writes its binary under the file name 'runner' regardless of what it contains, which is a naming artefact of internal/update and not a claim about cmd/runner. Measured limit: update.SwitchRollback is a stable-channel-only direction, so returning the preview channel is expressed as a forward move naming that version's own gate-passed candidate.

checks.name: A19-stability-probe
checks.summary: The full live argv was executed twice as two separate processes, each with -count=1, on the same commit (6888edf) and therefore the same candidate digests, and both verdicts are recorded. Run 1: sixteen of seventeen subtests passed and cap-autonomous-resolution FAILED -- the real claude invocation inside the runner-facing journey returned failure class provider-transport, code 1, retryable true, which the ledger records as a settled entry with no session_id and no usage counts. Run 2: all seventeen subtests passed, including cap-autonomous-resolution with session_id 11f82069-5fde-48f7-866a-cd577d76b82a. The two runs therefore DISAGREE on the cap-autonomous-resolution sub-exercise. This check is recorded failed so the disagreement cannot be read as a clean pair. Handling followed A19 exactly: the affected capability's check is recorded failed with both observations transcribed, no evidence id is written for it, both records' result stays partial, the first observation was neither deleted nor overwritten, and nothing was quarantined. A THIRD run exists and it is not a tie-breaker; the tie stands unbroken and cap-autonomous-resolution remains recorded failed. Its reason is separate and is stated so it cannot be misread: after the two runs, devbox run --pure -- make format reported that internal/api/live_dogfood_test.go needed gofmt (two struct-literal alignment lines, a whitespace-only diff of six changed lines). make check runs make format, so commit A could not be green without the fix, and fixing it changed a file the exercise compiles, which under the 2026-08-25 revision of gate rule G6 (G6b) forces re-observation regardless of the reason. The fix was applied, commit A was rebuilt as 39d2e80 with the same content plus that whitespace, and one confirming run was executed there: all seventeen subtests passed, including cap-autonomous-resolution. The gofmt change provably cannot alter any candidate digest, because internal/** is not a release bundle member (the seven roles are contracts/**, ci/components.json, go.mod, go.sum, devbox.lock, firestore.indexes.json, devbox.json, firebase.json and docs/preview|stable/**.md), and the measured bundle, contract and doc-set digests are byte-identical before and after it. A SECOND run at 39d2e80 was NOT made, and this is the honest reason: the V2-022 ledger stands at 23 of its 24-invocation runaway threshold, so a second full run (three accounted invocations) cannot be admitted. Reaching a threshold is a fail-closed stop for inspection and is neither a success nor a capability failure; the record's limits were not edited, the ledger was not edited or reinitialised, halted was not cleared, and no limit was raised. The consequence is stated plainly rather than papered over: the two-run stability probe stands at 6888edf on identical candidate digests, and the final commit A carries one confirming run plus a whitespace-only difference from the probed commit. This is escalated to the tech lead, together with the transient disagreement, rather than decided here.

checks.name: A21-two-commits
checks.summary: Two commits, in this order, and no others. Commit A (39d2e80) carries internal/api/live_dogfood_test.go, internal/contracts/capability_evidence_test.go, the two un-pinned internal/release test literals, the A14 release rename with evidence_ids still empty, every documentation change and the A2 preflight record; devbox run --pure -- go test ./..., devbox run --pure -- go vet ./..., devbox run --pure -- make format, make lint, make contracts, make docs, make ownership and the touched component targets (component-api, component-release, component-contracts, component-docs) are all green on its committed state, and the A22 composite evidence_key was read at that green tree. Commit B carries contracts/release-contract/foundation.json's evidence_ids, the two evidence records and their two index.json entries together, because clause f requires an evidence id to resolve in the index and splitting them makes the ledger test red in between. make check itself was not run by this task at the coordinator's instruction; go test ./..., go vet ./..., the make targets listed above and gitleaks over committed history are the substituted verification and that substitution is recorded rather than hidden.
